key_equations_and_data: §2 master equation: DN_ij = Q[ g_ij·S(Φ_ij) + o_ij + n_ij ] — noise n_ij and post-NUC residual gain/offset g_ij, o_ij enter BEFORE quantisation Q; the noise stage must therefore run on the pre-quantised signal (radiance or electrons), never on quantised DN.

§10.2 seven-component NVESD 3D noise synthesis: σ_TVH i.i.d. Gaussian per pixel per frame; σ_VH one fixed 2-D Gaussian field, slowly drifting; σ_V one Gaussian per row, fixed; σ_H one Gaussian per column, fixed; σ_TV new Gaussian per row per frame; σ_TH new Gaussian per column per frame; σ_T one global Gaussian per frame.
§10.2 variance closure: σ_total² = σ_T² + σ_V² + σ_H² + σ_TV² + σ_TH² + σ_VH² + σ_TVH² (components independent, zero mean).

§10.2 starting ratios, uncooled LWIR after NUC, 'all in NETD units': σ_TVH:σ_VH:σ_H:σ_V = 1.0:0.3:0.15:0.08; cooled MWIR: σ_VH smaller, σ_TVH dominant. §12.2 config extends to tv 0.05, th 0.05, t 0.02.

§12.2 config fields (already present in configs/sensors/flir_boson_640_lwir.yaml): noise.netd_mk_at_300k (anchor, 'scales everything'); noise.ratios_3d.{tvh,vh,h,v,tv,th,t} relative to σ_TVH; noise.fpn_drift_tau_s; noise.bad_pixel_fraction; noise.bad_pixel_cluster_lambda. Adjacent nuc.{mode: shuttered|shutterless|ideal, ffc_interval_s, ffc_freeze_ms, residual_gain_ppm_per_k, residual_offset_mk_per_k}.

§9.4 NETD photon-count form (the one to implement): NETD = σ_N,total / (∂N_e/∂T), with ∂N_e/∂T = η·A_d·t_int·π·τ_opt/(4F²+1)·(∂L_q/∂T)_B and σ_N,total² = N_e + σ_dark² + σ_read² + σ_1/f². Aperture factor MUST come from irsim.optics (CLAUDE.md #5).

§9.4 bolometer equivalent (what the LWIR anchor actually uses): σ_L[W m⁻² sr⁻¹] = NETD[K] × (∂L/∂T)_B(300 K), where (∂L/∂T)_B = ∫R(λ)·∂B/∂T dλ (§3.4, tabulated alongside L_B by radiometry). Predicted NETD at any scene T: NETD(T) = σ_L / (∂L/∂T)_B(T).

§9.4 anchor workflow (steps 1-4): build the physical chain → compute predicted NETD at 300 K → scale noise terms so it equals netd_mk_at_300k → structure is physical, magnitude matches the device. Appendix A.7: NETD is anchored, not predicted.
§3.4 / §9.4 known answer [R9]: a real uncooled core measured ≈39 mK NETD at ambient and ≈23 mK against a 100 °C blackbody → NETD(373 K)/NETD(300 K) ≈ 0.59. Test band: 0.5-0.7.
§3.4 rule + CLAUDE.md #3: add noise in radiance or electron space, then convert; never Kelvin-space Gaussian noise on a temperature buffer.

§10.1 physical source table: photon shot Poisson ∝√N_e (dominant MWIR/SWIR by day); dark shot ∝√(i_d·t_int/q); Johnson Gaussian √(4k_B·T·R·Δf) (bolometer dominant); temperature fluctuation √(4k_B·T²·G_th·Δf) (bolometer physical floor); read/ROIC Gaussian constant; 1/f pink; FPN gain+offset fixed spatial, scene-dependent, dominant after NUC decay.

§10.3 temporal structure: fixed-pattern terms evolve by a slow random walk with correlation time seconds-to-minutes (config fpn_drift_tau_s = 120 s) producing 'pattern breathing' between NUC events; temporal stripe noise modelled as a 1-D Gaussian along one image axis [R30].

§10.4 bad pixels: types dead (stuck low), hot (stuck high), flickering (random telegraph noise), blinking (intermittent); 0.05-0.5 % of pixels; Poisson cluster process (not uniform); camera replaces them by neighbour interpolation leaving a detectable smoothed footprint — simulate BOTH defect and replacement.

§11.2 NUC residual (shared with isp): DN_corr = G_ij(DN_ij − O_ij), G_ij = (mean DN^H − mean DN^L)/(DN^H_ij − DN^L_ij), O_ij = DN^L_ij; residual drift ∝ (T_FPA − T_FPA^cal) with config slopes residual_gain_ppm_per_k and residual_offset_mk_per_k; residual non-uniformity grows between FFC events; FFC event freezes the image 0.5-1 s (ffc_freeze_ms) and resets the pattern.

§8.2 self-emission Φ_self ≈ A_d·Ω_eff·(1−τ_opt)·L_B(T_housing), Ω_eff = π/(4F²+1) — the PHYSICAL origin of global offset drift; the noise area must not duplicate this as random walk (only pixel-level pattern drift is the noise area's).
sensor-noise-chain skill: seed all noise deterministically from (frame_id, sensor_id); §13.2 the SPG Lua global rtx.frameId is the engine-side frame id source.

§15 Tier 2 bench formulas: NETD_meas = ΔT·σ_noise/ΔDN from two blackbodies a few K apart, must match datasheet within 10 % and must fall with scene T; 3D-noise decomposition of 100+ frames of a uniform blackbody into σ_TVH, σ_VH, σ_V, σ_H [R28]; skill: synthesise with known ratios, decompose 200 frames, recover within 5 %.

§15 Tier 4(c): noise power spectral density of a flat region, shape within a factor of 2 across spatial frequency — needs a PSD utility (spatial 2-D PSD with row/column line extraction, temporal PSD per pixel).

§12.1 band table: dominant noise is shot for NIR/SWIR/MWIR and Johnson+FPN for LWIR — the noise stage must select electron-space (photon FPA) vs radiance-space (bolometer) from fpa.type, with no band-specific code.

tests/conftest.py fixtures the tests must use: gbuffer_uniform (64x64, 300 K float32) for decomposition/NETD benches, gbuffer_ramp (256x256, 250-450 K) for gain-residual and replacement tests, rng seed 20260910.
Physical constants needed (all already in irsim.radiometry.constants): K_BOLTZMANN, Q_E. No new constants required; RNG seeds and default cluster radius are parameters, not constants.

work_items.title: Bad-pixel map generation by a Poisson cluster process
work_items.description: `irsim.noise.bad_pixels.generate_map(shape, cfg, sensor_rng) -> BadPixelMap` (int8 type map: 0 good, 1 dead, 2 hot, 3 flicker, 4 blink). Neyman-Scott/Matérn: parent centres Poisson with intensity chosen so the expected total = fraction·H·W; each parent spawns 1 + Poisson(cluster_lambda) offspring within a small radius (define in ADR-5); types drawn from `bad_pixel_type_mix`. Map is fixed per sensor (not per frame).

work_items.title: Bad-pixel defect injection (dead/hot/RTS/blink) and camera neighbour-interpolation replacement
work_items.description: `apply_defects(frame, map, rts_state, frame_rng)`: dead → floor value, hot → ceiling value (in the frame's unit; when applied on DN, 0 and 2^bits−1), flicker → two-state random telegraph with per-frame switch probabilities, blink → intermittent with duty cycle; RTS/blink states persist in a `BadPixelState`. `replace(frame, map)`: mean of valid 4-neighbours (excluding other bad pixels, iterating until clusters are filled). Both live in irsim.noise because the footprint depends on the map; isp only sequences the call.

work_items.title: Electron-space noise for photon FPAs: shot, dark shot, read; anchor rule for shot-limited devices
work_items.description: `irsim.noise.photon.electron_noise(N_e, i_dark, t_int, sigma_read, rng)`: Poisson(N_e) + Poisson(i_dark·t_int/q) + Gaussian(σ_read); `predicted_netd_photon(N_e, σ_dark, σ_read, σ_1f, dNe_dT)`. The anchor scales only the non-shot terms (read, 1/f, FPN); if shot noise alone exceeds the datasheet NETD, raise with a message (ADR-6). ∂N_e/∂T uses irsim.optics aperture factor. Needed for SWIR/MWIR (§16.4 step 10), so it can be scheduled late.
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: test_shot_variance_equals_mean: N_e = 1e4, 1e5 samples: variance/mean = 1 within 2 % (Poisson identity)

test_predicted_netd_matches_bench: for a synthetic InGaAs-like config, NETD from the two-blackbody bench in electrons equals predicted_netd_photon within 10 %
test_shot_limited_anchor_raises: datasheet NETD below the shot-noise floor raises instead of silently producing negative read noise

work_items.title: Noise PSD diagnostics (spatial 2-D with row/column lines, temporal per pixel) for Tier 4(c)
work_items.description: `irsim.noise.analysis.spatial_psd(frame_or_cube)` (radially averaged plus the k_v = 0 and k_h = 0 lines where column/row noise concentrates) and `temporal_psd(cube)`. Pure analysis, no synthesis; later used to compare against real FLIR ADK flat regions with the factor-of-2 target. Also a `compare_psd(a, b) -> max ratio` helper.
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: test_white_noise_psd_is_flat: 200-frame average radial PSD of pure σ_TVH: max/min over 10 radial bins < 1.3 (χ² spread bound; fails if the FFT is un-normalised or windowed asymmetrically)
test_column_noise_lives_on_the_kv0_line: σ_H-only cube: ≥ 95 % of total power on the k_v = 0 line
test_ou_drift_temporal_psd_is_lorentzian: temporal PSD of a drifted VH pixel has −3 dB corner at f_c = 1/(2πτ) within 20 % (fails if the drift is white or a random walk)

work_items.title: Golden regression fixture for the Boson NoiseStage
work_items.description: Store an 8-frame 64x64 float32 cube produced by NoiseStage from configs/sensors/flir_boson_640_lwir.yaml with sensor_seed 20260910, plus a sidecar with the config SHA-256 and numpy version; test compares with 1e-6 relative tolerance, reports stale-vs-failing, writes the actual array beside the expected one on failure. Regenerated only via `make golden-update`.
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: test_boson_noise_golden: cube matches the stored reference to 1e-6 relative (catches any unintended change in seeding, ordering or magnitude; would also flag a NumPy stream change, which the sidecar distinguishes from a physics change)

work_items.title: Warp noise kernel (pipeline stage 5) mirroring NoiseStage, validated statistically against the CPU reference
work_items.description: In src/irsim_isaac/pipeline/noise_warp.py: a Warp kernel applying T/V/H/TV/TH/VH/TVH + residual + defects on GPU arrays, with persistent GPU buffers for fixed patterns, drift and RTS state held by a Python-side object; seeded from the annotator frame index (or rtx.frameId when in SPG). Because Gaussian transforms differ between NumPy and curand/Warp, agreement is statistical, not bit-exact (ADR-4).

tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: test_gpu_vs_cpu_3d_ratios (@pytest.mark.gpu): decompose_3d on 200 GPU frames recovers the CPU-reference sigmas within 5 % (TVH, VH, H) — fails if any component is missing, mis-scaled, or axes swapped on the GPU
test_gpu_netd_bench (@pytest.mark.gpu): two-blackbody bench on GPU output within 10 % of 50 mK
test_gpu_state_persists (@pytest.mark.gpu): frame 2's fixed pattern correlates with frame 1's at r > 0.999 (fails if the pattern is regenerated per dispatch)

tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: test_spg_vs_cpu_3d_ratios (@pytest.mark.isaac): captured 200-frame cube decomposes to the CPU sigmas within 5 % (TVH, VH, H), NETD bench within 10 %
test_spg_frameid_reproducibility (@pytest.mark.isaac): replaying the timeline from frame 0 twice yields bit-identical stage-5 outputs for the memoryless components

decisions_needing_adr.title: Which sigma the datasheet NETD anchors (σ_TVH, temporal σ, or σ_total) and at what reference conditions
decisions_needing_adr.why: §10.2 line 725 says the ratios are 'in NETD units' (i.e. σ_TVH = 1 NETD), §9.4 line 669 and the skill line 59 define NETD from σ_total, and §15 line 1191 measures ΔT·σ_noise/ΔDN without saying which σ. For the Boson ratios the choices differ by 6 % (σ_total/σ_TVH = 1.060), within the 10 % bench tolerance but outside the 5 % component tolerance, so every downstream test depends on this. It also decides whether the config NETD refers to the configured lens F or a datasheet reference F (NETD ∝ F², §8.1 line 525).
options: σ_TVH = NETD (matches §10.2 wording and per-pixel temporal NETD as FLIR measures it after NUC)
σ_total = NETD (matches the §9.4 formula literally; makes ratios shrink σ_TVH below the datasheet figure)
temporal σ = sqrt(σ_TVH²+σ_TV²+σ_TH²+σ_T²) = NETD (matches what a per-pixel temporal std over frames on a real camera returns)
add netd_ref_f_number to the config and rescale by (F_cfg/F_ref)² so lens trades change NETD

decisions_needing_adr.title: Noise-injection domain and unit per detector class
decisions_needing_adr.why: CLAUDE.md #3 forbids Kelvin-space noise but leaves radiance vs electrons vs pre-quantised DN open. Bolometers have no electron count, photon FPAs do; §2 places n_ij before Q. The choice fixes the interface of NoiseStage.apply and how sigmas are converted (dLb_dT vs ∂N_e/∂T).
options: band radiance (W m⁻² sr⁻¹) for bolometers and electrons for photon FPAs, converted by the respective derivative — unit-agnostic core
always electrons/'signal units' after S(Φ) with the detector supplying ∂S/∂T
always pre-quantised DN with gain from the detector

decisions_needing_adr.title: Temporal evolution of fixed-pattern terms: OU mean-reverting vs pure random walk vs 1/f-shaped; and which components drift
decisions_needing_adr.why: §10.3 says 'slow random walk' but a true random walk has unbounded variance and would silently break the configured 3D ratios over long runs; §10.2 says only σ_VH drifts while §10.3 says 'the fixed-pattern terms' (plural); §10.1/§10.2 fold 1/f into σ_VH, which an OU process approximates with a Lorentzian rather than 1/f spectrum. §8.2 line 543 additionally warns that global drift should come physically from Φ_self(T_housing), not from an arbitrary random walk — the ADR must state that the noise-area drift is pixel-level only.
options: OU on VH, V, H with one τ = fpn_drift_tau_s (stationary, ratios preserved, Lorentzian temporal PSD)
OU on VH only, V/H frozen until FFC
sum of 2-3 OU processes with spread τ to approximate 1/f over 0.01-10 Hz (higher fidelity, more state)
pure random walk with reset at FFC (literal spec, variance grows between FFC events)

decisions_needing_adr.title: RNG scheme and GPU reproducibility contract
decisions_needing_adr.why: The skill requires seeding from (frame_id, sensor_id); the spec seeds SPG from rtx.frameId. NumPy PCG64 + ziggurat cannot be reproduced bit-for-bit in CUDA/Warp; a counter-based Philox stream could match the 32-bit integers but not the Gaussian transform. The decision fixes whether golden tests are CPU-only and whether GPU tests are statistical (5 %/10 %) — and how frame_id, sensor_id and stream are combined (SeedSequence spawn vs hash).
options: NumPy SeedSequence(sensor_seed, frame_id, stream) + PCG64 on CPU; GPU statistically equivalent only
Philox counter-based on both sides with Box-Muller implemented identically for bit-exact CPU/GPU
hash-based per-pixel RNG (e.g. PCG hash of (x, y, frame, stream)) implemented identically in NumPy and CUDA

decisions_needing_adr.title: Bad-pixel cluster process definition, type mix, RTS/blink parameters and replacement stencil
decisions_needing_adr.why: §10.4 only says 'Poisson cluster process' and lists four types; the config's bad_pixel_cluster_lambda has no stated meaning; switching rates, cluster radius, type proportions and the interpolation kernel (4- vs 8-neighbour, cluster handling) are all unspecified yet determine the footprint that Tier 4/5 say perception networks latch onto.
options: Neyman-Scott: parents Poisson, 1+Poisson(λ) offspring within radius 2 px; mix dead 0.4/hot 0.4/flicker 0.1/blink 0.1; 4-neighbour mean excluding bad neighbours, iterated
Matérn cluster with uniform disc radius from config
explicit measured map loaded from a file for a specific unit (data/bad_pixels/<sensor>.npy), generator as fallback

decisions_needing_adr.title: Physical noise sources are not synthesised individually; magnitude comes from the NETD anchor (fidelity deliberately skipped)
decisions_needing_adr.why: §10.1 lists Johnson, temperature-fluctuation, dark-shot and 1/f with formulas, but §9.4 and Appendix A.7 anchor to the datasheet and the config carries no R, Δf or G_th. The ADR must state that bolometer noise is anchored-only, that photon shot noise IS physical and not rescaled (only read/1/f/FPN absorb the anchor), and what happens when the datasheet NETD is below the shot floor.
options: anchor-only for bolometers; physical shot + anchored residual for photon FPAs; raise if infeasible
add g_th_w_per_k and Δf to the fpa schema and assert config NETD ≥ temperature-fluctuation floor as a sanity check
full first-principles synthesis (Appendix A.7 says out of scope)

decisions_needing_adr.title: Module ownership split for NUC residual, bad-pixel replacement and the FFC freeze between irsim.noise and irsim.isp
decisions_needing_adr.why: CLAUDE.md layout assigns 'NUC residual' to noise/ and 'NUC' to isp/; §11.1 places bad-pixel replacement and NUC in the post-ADC signal chain while §13.4 SPG#5 (noise) does 'NUC residual + bad pixels' before SPG#6 (isp); §10.4 says simulate defect AND replacement in the noise section. Two teams could implement the same thing twice or leave the freeze unowned.
options: noise owns residual pattern, defects and replacement footprint; isp owns 2-pt correction arithmetic and the ffc_freeze_ms image hold; pipeline sequences the FFC event
isp owns everything after quantisation including replacement, noise only injects defects
a single 'fpa_behaviour' module spanning both

decisions_needing_adr.title: Spatial whiteness of σ_VH and σ_TVH
decisions_needing_adr.why: §10.2 synthesises σ_VH as a Gaussian field (implicitly white). Real bolometer FPN and the post-NUC residual have some spatial correlation, and §15 Tier 4(c) compares PSD shape within a factor of 2. Choosing white now is fine but must be recorded so the PSD comparison knows what to revisit.
options: white (i.i.d.) VH and TVH — spec-literal, revisit when Tier 4 PSD fails
optional low-pass (1-2 px Gaussian) on VH with a config knob
PSD-shaped synthesis from a measured spectrum file

ambiguities_and_risks.description: NETD anchor target is ambiguous (σ_TVH vs σ_total vs temporal σ) — see ADR-1. The Boson ratios make the choices differ by 6 %, so a 5 % component test written against the wrong convention will fail for reasons that look like a bug.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Before NOISE-05, compute both conventions numerically for the Boson ratios, record the 6 % gap in the ADR, and write the bench test to assert against the chosen convention explicitly. Cross-check with how FLIR quotes Boson NETD (temporal, per pixel, after NUC, at F/1.0, 300 K scene) from the datasheet cited as [R38].

ambiguities_and_risks.description: The 3D-noise decomposition estimator is not given in the spec (it defers to [R28]). Naive directional-average estimators are biased by leakage of larger components (e.g. naive σ_V² picks up σ_VH²/W = 0.0014 against a true 0.0064 — an 11 % bias) and σ_T (0.02·σ_TVH) has a sampling error of ~5 % at 1σ with 200 frames. The skill's flat 'recover within 5 %' is not attainable for the small components.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Derive the leakage terms analytically for each of the seven estimators, implement bias correction in NOISE-04, and run the round trip over 20 seeds to measure the empirical spread; set per-component tolerances from that spread (TVH/VH/H 5 %, V/TV/TH 10 % or 0.01·σ_TVH, T 15 %) and document them in the test.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: `bad_pixel_cluster_lambda: 1.6` has no definition anywhere in the spec; `fpn_drift_tau_s` is not stated to apply to V and H as well as VH; flicker/blink switching rates and amplitudes are undefined; the replacement stencil is undefined.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Cannot be verified from the spec. Define each in ADR-3/ADR-5, put every new knob in NoiseConfig with a default, and confirm the resulting footprint against a real FLIR ADK flat region (Tier 4) when data is available; until then tests assert only self-consistency.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Double counting risk between the additive σ_VH (§10.2) and the multiplicative gain residual g_ij (§2, §11.2): on a uniform 300 K scene they are indistinguishable, so a uniform-field bench cannot detect that both were tuned to the same number.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Use gbuffer_ramp (250-450 K): the spatial std of the fixed pattern must grow with signal only through the gain term; NOISE-09's test_gain_residual_is_scene_dependent pins the slope, and the anchor must be defined on the uniform 300 K field so σ_VH is the post-NUC additive part only.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Whether the datasheet NETD absorbs the configured lens: NETD ∝ F² (§8.1). If the config lens is F/1.4 but the 50 mK figure was measured at F/1.0, anchoring at the configured F under-estimates noise by 2×.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Read the Boson datasheet [R38] for the NETD measurement conditions; add `netd_ref_f_number` (and scene T) to the schema and apply (F_cfg/F_ref)² in NOISE-05; test that changing f_number from 1.0 to 1.4 doubles the anchored σ.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Isaac Sim 6.0 SPG persistent state: the noise stage needs read-modify-write buffers that survive between frames (drift, RTS states, bolometer IIR). §13.2 documents `cuda.static` as a cache keyed on arguments, not as a writable persistent buffer; whether a `.cu.lua` script may keep a mutable device buffer across invocations is undocumented.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Write a minimal SPG shader whose Lua script allocates a 1-element buffer once and whose kernel increments it every frame; capture with FileCapture over 10 frames and check the counter reaches 10. If it fails, keep stage 5 in Path B (Warp) where Python owns the state, and record in ADR/README that SPG#5 is deferred.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: `rtx.frameId` semantics are unverified: is it monotonic per render product, does it reset on timeline stop/start, does it advance for unrendered frames? This decides whether seeding from it gives replayable noise.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Log rtx.frameId from a trivial SPG Lua script across timeline stop/play/reset and across two render products in Isaac Sim 6.0; if unreliable, pass an explicit frame counter as a value input instead.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: NumPy Generator stream stability: numpy documents that bit streams may change between major versions, so the golden fixture (NOISE-13) and bit-identical replay tests could break on an upgrade and look like a physics regression.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Store the numpy version in the golden sidecar and pin numpy in the dev extras; the golden test must report 'stale (numpy version changed)' distinctly from 'failing'.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Unit-suite time budget (< 30 s total): decomposition and drift tests need hundreds of frames; at 640x512 that is tens of MB per 100 frames and seconds per test.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Keep all unit benches at gbuffer_uniform's 64x64 (200 frames = 0.8 M samples) or 32x32 for the 3000-frame drift test; time the suite in CI and mark any full-resolution bench @pytest.mark.slow.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Quantisation LSB vs NETD: §2 puts noise before Q, but if the detector's 16-bit range spans the full 200-1000 K LUT the LSB in kelvin-equivalent could approach the NETD and the DN-domain bench would read a quantisation-inflated NETD.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: In the detector config validation assert LSB (in mK via dLb_dT at 300 K) < NETD/4; NOISE-10's DN bench should also be run against the radiance-domain bench and agree within 3 %.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Bad-pixel replacement algorithms of real cores are proprietary; the footprint we simulate (4-neighbour mean) may differ in shape from the Boson's, and §10.4 says the footprint is what perception sees.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Tier 4: locate replaced pixels in real ADK frames (they appear as local Laplacian minima at fixed positions) and compare the edge-spread of the footprint with the simulated one; adjust the stencil in ADR-5 if the shape differs.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: The temperature-fluctuation floor √(4k_B T² G_th Δf) (§10.1) cannot be evaluated because G_th and Δf are not in the fpa schema; a config NETD below the physical floor would go unnoticed.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Decide in ADR-6 whether to add g_th_w_per_k and bandwidth_hz to the schema; if added, write a test that the Boson config's 50 mK is above the computed floor (expected a few mK for 12 µm VOx at 30 Hz).

ambiguities_and_risks.description: conftest.py says 'Every test that uses randomness must take this [rng fixture]' while the skill says seed from (frame_id, sensor_id); tests that construct NoiseStage with an explicit sensor_seed will not use the fixture.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Agree the convention in the first noise PR: physics tests seed via the stage API with a literal seed; the rng fixture is for ad-hoc sampling. Update the conftest docstring accordingly.

non_negotiables_touched: #1 Engine-free core: all of NOISE-01..13 live in src/irsim/noise and import only numpy/scipy/pydantic; tests/unit/test_layering.py is parametrised over every src/irsim/*.py so new files are checked automatically. Warp/SPG code (NOISE-14/15) goes in src/irsim_isaac only.

#2 float32 or better everywhere: NoiseStage asserts float32 input/output and float32 persistent state (fixed patterns, drift, residual fields); NOISE-10 test_float32_boundary rejects float16 input; NOISE-03 test_output_is_float32; golden fixture stored as float32 .npy. Drift accumulation in float32 checked for zero-mean by NOISE-06 test_mean_stays_zero.

#3 Noise in radiance/electron space, never Kelvin: NOISE-05 converts netd_mk_at_300k to radiance via (∂L/∂T)_B(300 K) and the tests test_netd_falls_with_scene_temperature (ratio in [0.5, 0.7], identity to dLb_dT ratio) and test_kelvin_sigma_not_constant would both pass trivially at 1.0 — i.e. fail — if noise were added in Kelvin. NOISE-11 does the electron-space equivalent for photon FPAs.

#5 Aperture factor π/(4F²+1) from irsim.optics only: NOISE-11's ∂N_e/∂T must import optics.aperture_factor; test_aperture_factor_plus_one detects the 20 % difference at F/1.0. Note §9.4's datasheet form (4F²) is not to be implemented.

#6 One WeatherSeries: not directly touched, but NOISE-09 must take T_FPA from the detector's FPA thermal model (which derives ambient from the single WeatherSeries) rather than accepting an independent ambient temperature; the NucResidual API takes T_FPA as an input scalar, never weather.
spec_internal_inconsistencies: §9.4 line 661 quotes the datasheet NETD form with 4F² (NETD = 4F²V_n/(R·A_d·L')) while §2 line 112, §9.4 line 671 (photon-count form) and CLAUDE.md non-negotiable #5 mandate π/(4F²+1). Only the photon-count form should be coded; the 4F² form is a quotation of [R26].

§10.2 line 725 defines the ratio table 'all in NETD units' with σ_TVH = 1.0 (NETD anchors σ_TVH), but §9.4 lines 669-674 define NETD = σ_N,total/(∂N_e/∂T) with σ_total including every term, and the skill line 59 repeats 'NETD = σ_total / (∂N_e/∂T)'. For the Boson ratios σ_total = 1.060·σ_TVH — the two definitions differ by 6 %.

§10.2 table lines 708-716 lists seven components; line 725 gives starting ratios for only four (TVH, VH, H, V); §12.2 lines 865-872 and the Boson YAML add tv 0.05, th 0.05, t 0.02 with no source. §15 line 1192 asks to decompose only four components (σ_TVH, σ_VH, σ_V, σ_H) while the skill line 164 says 'recover the ratios within 5 %' for all synthesised ratios; 5 % is statistically unattainable for σ_T = 0.02 from 200 frames.

§10.3 line 731 prescribes a 'slow random walk' for fixed-pattern terms, §10.2 line 711 says 'slowly drifting', and §8.2 line 543 says that if you model optics self-emission 'you get NUC behaviour for free; skip it and you have to fake NUC drift with an arbitrary random walk' — the spec both mandates and disparages the random walk. Resolution: pixel-level pattern drift (noise area) and global offset drift from Φ_self(T_housing) (optics area) are different effects; a pure random walk also violates the stationary variance implied by fixed ratios.
§10.3 says only that fixed-pattern 'terms' drift; §10.2 line 711 marks only σ_VH as drifting while σ_V (line 712) and σ_H (line 713) are 'fixed'. The config exposes a single fpn_drift_tau_s.

Module ownership: CLAUDE.md layout gives noise/ '3D noise model, FPN, bad pixels, NUC residual' and isp/ 'NUC, AGC, DDE, palette'. §11 line 745 says the signal chain is 'everything after the ADC' and §11.1 line 750 puts 'bad-pixel replace → NUC' there, whereas §13.4 lines 1018-1019 put '3D noise + NUC residual + bad pixels' in SPG#5 (noise) before SPG#6 (isp), and §10.4 line 738 puts the replacement in the noise section. §2 line 70 places g_ij, o_ij and n_ij before Q (pre-ADC), which contradicts 'after the ADC' for the residual.

§16.4 step 4 (line 1301) is 'Detector + 3D noise + NETD calibration' and step 9 (line 1306) is 'Bolometer time constant, NUC/FFC, bad pixels', but the §1 fidelity ladder (line 54) makes 'full FPA chain + 3D noise' the L2 target and lists 'bolometer dynamics' as L3 (line 55) — the build order includes an L3 item before the L2 second band, while the skill's test list (line 165) treats bolometer smear as a core noise-chain test. Bolometer IIR is detector-area work, not noise; planners should not schedule it under noise.

§10.1 line 700 says FPN is 'scene-dependent' (multiplicative gain non-uniformity) but the §10.2 synthesis recipe is purely additive; scene dependence only enters through g_ij in §2 / the §11.2 gain residual — the spec never says which module carries it, creating a double-counting hazard.

§10.1 gives explicit formulas for Johnson (√(4k_B T R Δf)) and temperature-fluctuation (√(4k_B T² G_th Δf)) noise but neither §12.2 nor the Boson YAML carries R, Δf or G_th, and Appendix A.7 line 1392 states NETD is anchored, not predicted — the formulas cannot be evaluated from the config as specified.

tests/conftest.py line 13 docstring: 'Every test that uses randomness must take this [rng fixture]' conflicts with the skill line 101 'Seed all noise deterministically from (frame_id, sensor_id)' — the stage API will carry its own seeds and most noise tests will not use the fixture.

§13.2 line 959 and the isaac skill line 50 seed temporal noise from rtx.frameId only; the skill's (frame_id, sensor_id) rule needs a per-camera identifier that §13 never provides for multi-camera (TiledCameraSensor, §13.8) setups.
